snippets.headline: Poor control patients count A1c-tested patients whose latest measurement-year A1c exceeds 9.0 percent.

It represents patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is `> 9.0%`; the threshold is strict, so exactly 9.0 is not included. Query it as `MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`)`, for example `SELECT `Clinic`, MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`) AS `poor_control_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: Patient-level A1c results classify patients into no-result, good-control, poor-control, or intermediate-control bands.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The patient-level GSD A1c control band is derived from `gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value`. snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: The business term `GSD` means glycemic status, specifically A1c testing. In the care-gap logic, a GSD row with `status = 'NOT_MET'` receives the exact gap reason `'No A1c test in year'`. snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics`, `Good Control Patients` is a predefined measure with definition-time expression `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value < 8.0)` over the source. snippets.content: `Gap Reason` is a live dimension defined over the source as `CASE WHEN evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met' ELSE 'No A1c test in measurement year' END`. To group care gaps by reason, select `` `Gap Reason` `` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics` and group with the selected measures using `GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: Elevated glycemic trigger events are patient measurements above nine with follow-up assessed during the subsequent ninety days.
snippets.content: For calendar year 2025, a trigger event is an HbA1c observation whose modeled-or-raw value is `> 9` and whose description does NOT match the case-insensitive regular expression `recheck`. HbA1c observations are identified by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation o` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts lp` on `o.loinc_code = lp.loinc_code` with `lp.part = 'LP-HBA1C' AND lp.predicate = 'has_component'`. pages_read.body:
**GSD (Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes)** is a HEDIS quality measure of glycemic control:
it reads each eligible patient's **last** A1c of the measurement year.

- **Eligible population (denominator):** patients aged **18–75** as of the end of the measurement year who
  are in the **diabetes cohort** (an ICD-10-CM diabetes diagnosis under E10/E11/E13, resolved by subsumption
  over the ICD-10 hierarchy).
- **Two HEDIS indicators, both over all eligible patients:** **good control** = last A1c **below 8.0%**;
  **poor control** = last A1c **above 9.0%, or no A1c test** in the measurement year (a missing test counts as
  poor control; lower is better). A1c tests are the LOINC value set `GSD_A1C_TEST`.
- **Compliant (Blood Sugar Controlled):** last A1c **9.0% or below**, the inverse of the poor-control indicator.

A patient is **MET** when their last A1c is 9.0% or below, otherwise **NOT_MET** (a care gap: above 9.0% or no test).
In `gsd_compliance_metrics`: **GSD Compliance Rate** (compliant ÷ eligible), **Good Control Rate**, **Poor Control
Rate**, and **Tested Patients** (testing coverage, not a HEDIS indicator).

> HEDIS-aligned demo, not NCQA-certified. GSD replaced the older "HbA1c Control for Patients With Diabetes"
> framing in recent HEDIS measurement years.

**Related assets:** `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd`, `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics`

 COUNT_IF(`evidence_value` > 9) AS last_a1c_gt9,

FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_adherence_gsd`
WHERE `measurement_year` = 2026
GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY poor_control_pct DESC

snippets.headline: Patient-level A1c results classify patients into no-result, good-control, poor-control, or intermediate-control bands.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)

snippets.headline: Cardiorenal patients are the intersection of diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure clinical evidence.
snippets.content: A cardiorenal patient is a `patient_id` in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition with evidence of all three diagnosis groups: diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure. The ICD-10 prefix implementation is `icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'` for diabetes, `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'` for chronic kidney disease, and `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'` for heart failure. The cohort is the intersection of patients meeting all three conditions, implemented either as three joined distinct patient sets or as flags requiring `has_dm = 1 AND has_ckd = 1 AND has_hf = 1`. Do not count a patient with only one or two of the three diagnosis groups as cardiorenal.

snippets.headline: Qualifying complications include diabetes kidney, eye, and other specified complication descendants under nine explicitly listed ancestor codes.
snippets.content: A patient is classified as having a qualifying complication when `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` contains an `icd10_code` whose closure match in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` has `ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`. The full included ancestor-code list is exactly `('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2','E11.3','E10.3','E13.3','E11.4','E10.4','E13.4')`; no other ancestor codes are included by this rule. The complication cohort is deduplicated with `SELECT DISTINCT c.patient_id` before it is used in the clinic metric.

snippets.headline: Diabetes quality reporting covers five HEDIS aligned demonstration measures, with patient evidence tables and governed views for rates.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)

The metric views expose Measurement Year, Compliance Status, Age Band and Measure dimensions; MET / NOT_MET logic resides in Compliance Status. The diabetes cohort uses subsumption over the ICD-10-CM hierarchy under E10/E11/E13.

snippets.headline: ICD-10 closure maps raw diagnosis codes to diabetes ancestor families before counting distinct patient diagnosis codes.
snippets.content: To relate raw encounter diagnosis codes to ICD-10 ancestry, join `care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx b` to `care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure cl` with `cl.descendant_code = b.icd10_code`. The diabetes ancestry lookup filters the closure table with INCLUDE list `cl.ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`; those are the complete ancestor codes shown. The query counts `COUNT(DISTINCT b.icd10_code)` after the join, so the metric is the number of distinct raw diagnosis codes for the patient that roll up to those diabetes ancestors, not a count of encounters or closure rows. A patient filter remains on the raw diagnosis table as `b.patient_id = h.pid`, and the closure table contributes the ancestor classification.

snippets.headline: The target population consists of distinct patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses.
snippets.content: The clinical cohort is the set of DISTINCT `patient_id` values appearing in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` under all three diagnosis conditions: `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'` for diabetes, `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'` for chronic kidney disease, and `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'` for heart failure. The three diagnosis subsets are joined with INNER JOIN on `patient_id`, so a patient must have at least one matching diagnosis in each subset. The cohort count is `COUNT(*)` over the resulting distinct patient list, not a count of diagnosis records.

snippets.headline: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort includes patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses together.
snippets.content: The cardio-renal diabetes cohort is defined from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx at the distinct `patient_id` grain. A patient is INCLUDED only when they have at least one diagnosis code matching each of these three required groups: diabetes `icd10_code LIKE 'E11%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E10%' OR icd10_code LIKE 'E13%'`, chronic kidney disease `icd10_code LIKE 'N18%'`, and heart failure `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'`. The cohort construction uses INNER JOINs among the three distinct patient lists, so missing any one group excludes the patient. Because the diagnosis table can contain multiple encounter rows per patient, deduplicate to `SELECT DISTINCT patient_id` for each condition group before joining or aggregating.

snippets.headline: Text-based cardiorenal membership searches diagnosis descriptions but still requires all three clinical conditions.
snippets.content: A description-based cardiorenal cohort uses text matching in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition instead of ICD hierarchy matching. INCLUDE diabetes patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%diabetes%'`, chronic kidney disease patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%chronic kidney%' OR lower(description) LIKE '%ckd%'`, and heart failure patients with `lower(description) LIKE '%heart failure%'`. The cohort is still the intersection of all three distinct `patient_id` sets, joined on `patient_id`. This text-based rule is a separate cohort construction method from ICD-prefix or ICD-closure rules and can return different patients when descriptions and codes do not align.

snippets.headline: Hierarchy-based cardiorenal membership expands standard diagnosis families before requiring all three clinical conditions.
snippets.content: The hierarchy-based cardiorenal cohort expands diagnosis groups through eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure before matching eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition. INCLUDE diabetes descendants where `ancestor_code IN ('E10','E11','E13')`, chronic kidney disease descendants where `ancestor_code = 'N18'`, and heart failure descendants where `ancestor_code = 'I50'`; then require `silver_condition.icd10_code IN (SELECT descendant_code ...)` for each group. The final cohort is the INTERSECT of the three distinct patient sets, so all three diagnosis groups are required. This method should be kept separate from free-text description matching because it uses controlled ICD hierarchy membership rather than diagnosis text.

snippets.headline: Kidney complication count measures distinct patients whose diagnoses descend from three specified diabetes kidney complication ancestors.
snippets.content: The `kidney` measure is `COUNT(DISTINCT c.patient_id)` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition` joined to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure` on `c.icd10_code = cl.descendant_code`. Include only closure rows where `cl.ancestor_code IN ('E11.2','E10.2','E13.2')`; this is an INCLUDE filter, and the complete list contains exactly those three ancestor codes. The measure is patient-level and does not restrict diagnoses by measurement year or observation date in the demonstrated SQL.

snippets.headline: Diagnosis complications are classified into kidney, retinopathy, neuropathy, circulatory, or uncomplicated categories using code-pattern precedence.
snippets.content: The complication bucket is derived from the selected `dx_code` using this complete CASE mapping: `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.2%'` maps to `'kidney'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.3%'` maps to `'retinopathy'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.4%'` maps to `'neuropathy'`; `dx_code LIKE 'E1_.5%'` maps to `'circulatory'`; all other values map to `'uncomplicated'`. Because the CASE evaluates top to bottom, the first matching pattern determines `cx_bucket`. The classification is applied after the patient-level diagnosis reduction from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` and the adherence join to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd`.

snippets.headline: The cardiorenal cohort requires diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnoses for the same patient.
snippets.content: The cardiorenal patient count is the number of distinct patients present in all three diagnosis cohorts: diabetes, CKD, and heart failure. Diabetes is defined by `icd10_code RLIKE '^E1[013]'`, heart failure by `icd10_code LIKE 'I50%'`, and CKD by either the direct-prefix cohort or the closure-based cohort described separately. The query computes `COUNT(*)` after joining the already-distinct patient sets with `JOIN ... USING(patient_id)`, producing `cardiorenal_prefix` for diabetes intersected with direct-prefix CKD and heart failure, and `cardiorenal_closure` for diabetes intersected with closure-based CKD and heart failure. Because each cohort is deduplicated to one row per patient before joining, the intersection counts are patient counts rather than diagnosis-row counts.

Because the complication set is deduplicated by patient before the left join, a patient contributes 1.0 to every adherence clinic row when that patient has a qualifying complication; patients without a match contribute 0.0.

snippets.headline: The cardiorenal cohort includes patients with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure diagnosis evidence.
snippets.content: The cardiorenal cohort in `care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx` is an INNER intersection of three diagnosis-derived patient sets. Each set is deduplicated as `SELECT DISTINCT patient_id` before joining, so a patient qualifies once per condition regardless of multiple encounters or diagnoses. The final cohort is `SELECT patient_id FROM dm JOIN ckd USING(patient_id) JOIN hf USING(patient_id)`, requiring the same `patient_id` to appear in all three sets.

**About the date cutoff:**
- The cutoff doesn't remove anyone. The latest recorded onset date in the data is 2026-10-30, so "on or before 2026-10-30" covers every kidney-complication diagnosis on file. - No patient is missing an onset date.
- Onset dates go back to 1944, so this counts every patient with this diagnosis on record, not only new diagnoses in one measurement year.

snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Protocol Step-3 means A1c follow-up after a high result and uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics. It counts only closed 90-day follow-up windows, with Trigger Events as the denominator. Open Obligations identify high-A1c patients still closable this year and are surfaced for action questions. Recent months are not described as a decline because their windows are not yet closed.

snippets.headline: This metric view measures whether high A1c results receive timely follow-up, revealing protocol adherence by clinic and primary-care panel.
snippets.content: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics` is a Diabetes care-protocol Step 3 metrics view. The business question is whether an A1c result >= 9% (poor control) receives a follow-up A1c within 90 days; it is HEDIS-aligned for demonstration and is not NCQA-certified. Query the exposed dimensions and measures from this metrics view rather than treating it as a raw-row table, and use `MEASURE()` for every measure with `GROUP BY ALL`. Its underlying source is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_protocol_adherence` (ASSET).

snippets.headline: Good and poor glycemic control rates measure tested patients, whereas glycemic assessment compliance measures testing among all eligible patients.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: On eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, good control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value < 8.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL), and poor control is COUNT_IF(evidence_value > 9.0) / COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL). Both denominators count A1c-tested patient rows, unlike GSD compliance's COUNT(*) eligible-row denominator. Average latest A1c (%) is AVG(evidence_value); the supplied expression has no explicit evidence_datetime filter. The clinic example also reports COUNT(*) AS eligible_patients and COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) AS gsd_compliance_rate, GROUP BY clinic_id ORDER BY gsd_compliance_rate DESC, without a year filter. The verified poor-control sample uses MEASURE(`Poor Control Rate`) from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics. The poorly controlled patient filter INCLUDES evidence_value > 9.0.

snippets.headline: Elevated glycemic trigger events are patient measurements above nine with follow-up assessed during the subsequent ninety days.
snippets.content: For calendar year 2025, a trigger event is an HbA1c observation whose modeled-or-raw value is `> 9` and whose description does NOT match the case-insensitive regular expression `recheck`. The value is `CASE WHEN g.glycemic_poor AND g.modeled_a1c IS NOT NULL THEN g.modeled_a1c ELSE o.value_num END`, so a non-null modeled value replaces the raw observation value only for patients flagged `glycemic_poor`. HbA1c observations are identified by joining `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation o` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts lp` on `o.loinc_code = lp.loinc_code` with `lp.part = 'LP-HBA1C' AND lp.predicate = 'has_component'`. The year scope is `year(o.result_ts) = 2025`.

snippets.headline: Clinic protocol adherence is ranked by Step-3 A1c follow-up rate, with open obligations and follow-up timing reported alongside.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For clinic-level Step-3 A1c follow-up adherence, query `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics` and select `Clinic`, `MEASURE(``Trigger Events``) AS closed_triggers`, `MEASURE(``Followed Up In Time``) AS followed_up`, `MEASURE(``Protocol Step 3 Adherence Rate``) AS step3_adherence_rate`, `MEASURE(``Open Obligations``) AS open_obligations`, and `MEASURE(``Avg Days To Follow-up``) AS avg_days_to_followup`. Group by `Clinic` and order by `step3_adherence_rate` ascending to identify clinics with the lowest adherence. The same result reports trigger events, timely follow-ups, open obligations, and average days to follow-up for each clinic.

snippets.headline: Medication adherence covers adults with at least two metformin fills, and adherence requires medication coverage of at least eighty percent.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: MAD covers adults with at least two biguanide (metformin) fills; adherent means PDC >= 80 percent. The clinic query uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.mad_compliance_metrics with MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`), MEASURE(`Adherent Patients`), MEASURE(`MAD Adherence Rate`), and MEASURE(`Avg PDC`). It groups by Clinic and ORDER BY mad_adherence_rate, without an explicit year filter in this particular SQL example. The general latest-year default and the six-measure comparison use the GSD gold table for MAD's latest year.

snippets.headline: Patient-level A1c results classify patients into no-result, good-control, poor-control, or intermediate-control bands.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: The patient-level GSD A1c control band is derived from `gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value`. Use this exact expression: `CASE WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value IS NULL THEN 'No A1c' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value < 8 THEN 'Good control (<8%)' WHEN gold_adherence_gsd.evidence_value > 9 THEN 'Poor control (>9%)' ELSE '8-9%' END`. A missing value means `No A1c`; values below 8 are `Good control (<8%)`; values above 9 are `Poor control (>9%)`; all remaining non-null values, including 8 and 9, are `8-9%`.

snippets.headline: HEDIS diabetes quality uses five deterministic measures to assess eligible patients in synthetic, Epic-shaped data.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: The care protocol evaluates five HEDIS-aligned diabetes measures from synthetic, Epic-shaped data: GSD for glycemic status and A1c testing, KED for kidney health evaluation, BPD for blood-pressure control, SPD for statin therapy, and EED for diabetic eye examination. The population is described as 25,000 patients, but each measure's denominator is its own eligible-patient population. The data is explicitly not NCQA-certified and not for clinical use.

snippets.headline: Follow-up compliance counts qualifying recheck measurements after each trigger and excludes same-time or later-than-ninety-day results.
snippets.content: For each trigger row, follow-up is a qualifying HbA1c observation whose description matches `lower(coalesce(description,'')) RLIKE 'recheck'`, whose `result_ts` is strictly greater than the trigger timestamp, and whose elapsed time satisfies `datediff(followup_ts, trigger_ts) <= 90`. The event-level flag is `MAX(CASE WHEN f.fts > t.trigger_ts AND datediff(f.fts,t.trigger_ts)<=90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`, grouped by `patient_id, trigger_ts`; therefore multiple qualifying rechecks still produce one met/not-met result per trigger event. The published no-follow-up rate is `round(100.0*sum(1-met)/count(*),1)`, with the denominator equal to the number of trigger events, not distinct patients. Trigger events come from 2025 HbA1c observations in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation`, and follow-up observations use the same HbA1c terminology join through `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.loinc_parts`.

snippets.headline: Diabetes quality rates use governed measures, while patient care-gap worklists use evidence tables without stored compliance statuses.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: This supplied portion covers HEDIS diabetes quality and Step-3 follow-up over synthetic demo data. Rates, counts, numerators, and denominators come from named measures in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic metric views, using MEASURE(); rates are not re-derived by sums or averages or recomputed from gold tables. Patient detail comes from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_* evidence tables, which have no status column and already contain denominator-eligible rows. Results are HEDIS-aligned, not NCQA-certified; that qualification accompanies reported rates.

snippets.headline: Poor control patients count A1c-tested patients whose latest measurement-year A1c exceeds 9.0 percent.
snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics`, `Poor Control Patients` is a predefined measure with definition-time expression `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE evidence_value > 9.0)` over the source. It represents patients whose latest measurement-year A1c is `> 9.0%`; the threshold is strict, so exactly 9.0 is not included. Query it as `MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`)`, for example `SELECT `Clinic`, MEASURE(`Poor Control Patients`) AS `poor_control_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.gsd_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: The patient roster provides both a poor-glycemic flag and modeled HbA1c values used to characterize the 2025 patient panel.
snippets.content: The roster-level counts are `(SELECT count(*) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster WHERE glycemic_poor)` for patients flagged poor glycemic control and `(SELECT count(*) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster WHERE glycemic_poor AND modeled_a1c > 9)` for poor-glycemic patients whose modeled HbA1c exceeds 9. These are row counts from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.panel_roster`, not distinct patient counts, because the SQL uses `count(*)` rather than `count(DISTINCT patient_id)`. Use the first count for roster rows marked `glycemic_poor`; use the second for rows satisfying both `glycemic_poor` and `modeled_a1c > 9`.

snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: GSD means Glycemic Status Assessment: diabetics aged 18-75 with an A1c test in the measurement year. Patient-level clinic/panel compliance is COUNT_IF(evidence_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*) over eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd, with all patient rows in the breakdown as denominator. Care gaps INCLUDE evidence_datetime IS NULL. This testing rate differs from good and poor control rates, whose denominator is A1c-tested patients rather than all eligible patient rows.

These are the care-protocol knowledge edges, one sentence per edge. They are the same facts the knowledge graph
and `protocol_edges` hold: this Page is generated from `src/terminology/protocol_edges.csv` (`scripts/gen_protocol_pages.py`), so it can't drift from them. Synthetic demo protocol; not clinical guidance.

## Drug-class recommendations

- Statins are recommended for the SPD measure (statin therapy, ages 40-75). *(protocol section CP-DM-2025.1 sec2/sec6)*
- ACE inhibitors are recommended for albuminuria. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ARBs are recommended for albuminuria. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for chronic kidney disease (value set `COMORBID_CKD`). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended for heart failure (value set `COMORBID_HF`). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- Metformin (biguanide) is first-line for glucose lowering. *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*

## Contraindications

- Statins are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Statins are contraindicated with active hepatic disease (value set `CONTRA_HEPATIC`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ACE inhibitors are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- ARBs are contraindicated with pregnancy (value set `CONTRA_PREGNANCY`). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Metformin (biguanide) is contraindicated when eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m². *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*
- SGLT2 inhibitors are contraindicated when eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73m². *(protocol section CP sec4)*

## What each measure is monitored by

- GSD is monitored by HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- KED is monitored by eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- KED is monitored by uACR (LP-UACR). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- BPD is monitored by systolic blood pressure (LP-SBP). *(protocol section CP sec5)*
- BPD is monitored by diastolic blood pressure (LP-DBP). *(protocol section CP sec5)*

## Thresholds and definitions

- Albuminuria is defined by uACR of 30 mg/g or more. *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- BPD has the threshold systolic below 140 mmHg. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- BPD has the threshold diastolic below 90 mmHg. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- GSD has the threshold good control: A1c below 8%. *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- GSD has the threshold poor control: A1c above 9%. *(protocol section CP sec3)*

## Which lab each threshold is measured on

- Good control: A1c below 8% is measured on HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- Poor control: A1c above 9% is measured on HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C). *(protocol section CP sec3)*
- eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73m² is measured on eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP-GLY-2)*
- eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73m² is measured on eGFR (LP-EGFR). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- uACR of 30 mg/g or more is measured on uACR (LP-UACR). *(protocol section CP sec4)*
- Systolic below 140 mmHg is measured on systolic blood pressure (LP-SBP). *(protocol section CP sec2)*
- Diastolic below 90 mmHg is measured on diastolic blood pressure (LP-DBP). *(protocol section CP sec2)*

For the A1c recheck rule (Protocol Step 3) see the Page *Protocol Step 3 — A1c recheck within 90 days*.

## The care protocol doesn't set an A1c target for older adults with moderate comorbidity

The care protocol data has **no A1c target based on age or comorbidity**. None of its rules mention older adults, comorbidity level or an individualized glycemic goal. I searched all 29 rules in the protocol rules table and found nothing that matches. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/264d2c70dbe0445ea26370c622f7ecb7?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_d16a9d) [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/protocol_edges?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### A1c thresholds the protocol does define (same for every adult)

| Rule | Threshold | Protocol section |
|---|---|---|
| GSD good control | A1c **below 8%** | CP sec2 |
| GSD poor control | A1c **above 9%** | CP sec3 |
| Monitoring | HbA1c (LOINC part LP-HBA1C) | CP sec5 |

These match the published care-protocol rules glossary page. [Care-protocol rules (drug classes, contraindications, thresholds)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/e210469b-4179-45be-91f3-398359a04af3?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) The only rule tagged with version 2025.1 (section label "CP-DM-2025.1 sec2/sec6") recommends statins for SPD. It doesn't cover A1c. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/264d2c70dbe0445ea26370c622f7ecb7?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_d16a9d) Step 3 of the protocol adds a separate follow-up rule: after a high A1c result, the care team should intensify therapy and recheck A1c within 90 days. [Protocol Step 3 — A1c recheck within 90 days](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/240387f5-7f44-4dc6-9e12-08e037f2d00d?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

### What this means

- The closest answer is **below 8%**, the protocol's general "good control" threshold. It applies to everyone; it is not a target set for older patients with moderate comorbidity.
- A rule like "older adult, moderate comorbidity → A1c below X%" isn't recorded in the protocol rules, the glossary pages or the dashboards. If your v2025.1 protocol document includes one, it hasn't been loaded into this data, so I can't confirm the value.
- This is a synthetic demo protocol that is HEDIS-aligned but not NCQA-certified, and it is not clinical guidance. The matched observation codes are collected as a comma-separated distinct set with `concat_ws(', ', collect_set(o.loinc_code))`; this is a code-coverage result, not a count of observations. Value-set versions come from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` filtered with `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`, and each version is retained even when no 2025 patients match because the final joins are LEFT JOINs.

snippets.headline: Cross-year kidney evaluation comparisons can show an artificial decrease when later-year kidney test value sets retain only CKD-EPI evidence.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: A later measurement year's KED eGFR value set keeps only the CKD-EPI code. Cross-year KED comparisons can consequently show an artificial drop. The content provides no literal LOINC code or specific later year for this caveat.

snippets.headline: Each KED eGFR value-set version connects to observed patients through matching LOINC codes in the clinical observation records.
snippets.content: The complete relationship path for eGFR code matching is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` filtered by `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'` -> `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment.code` equals `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.loinc_code` -> observation patients via `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation.patient_id`. The SQL first derives distinct versions from `measurement_year`, then joins the version-and-code rows back on `measurement_year`, and finally LEFT JOINs observations on `loinc_code`; unmatched versions remain present with zero matching patients. Multiple code rows can match one version and multiple observations can match one code, so use `COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)` rather than counting joined rows to avoid code- and observation-level fanout.

snippets.headline: KED_EGFR terminology versions are compared by counting distinct patients with matching laboratory observations from calendar year 2025.
snippets.content: To calculate coverage for one terminology version, first select `measurement_year` values from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` where `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`, then use that same segment and `measurement_year` to obtain its complete code set. Join those codes to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` using `loinc_code = code` and restrict observations with `YEAR(result_ts) = 2025`. For the 2026 version specifically, include `measurement_year = '2026'` and compute `COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)`; the source uses a LEFT JOIN from the version/code set, so a version with no matching observations remains represented with a zero-like unmatched result rather than being removed by the join itself.

snippets.headline: KED compliance measures kidney-health testing for eligible diabetes patients aged 18 through 85 during each measurement year.
snippets.content: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics` is a HEDIS-aligned demonstration metrics view for Kidney Health Evaluation (KED), not an NCQA-certified measure. Its denominator is eligible diabetes patients aged 18-85, and full compliance requires BOTH an eGFR test and a uACR test in the measurement year. Query measures from the metrics view with `MEASURE()` and `GROUP BY ALL`; do not treat the view as an ordinary row-level table or reconstruct its measures with `SUM`/`COUNT`.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation performance includes both kidney testing components, with urine albumin testing usually identified as the limiting component.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED means kidney evaluation with eGFR and uACR components. Annual performance from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics groups by `Measurement Year` and selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`), MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`), and MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`). INCLUDE only `Measurement Year` = (SELECT MAX(measurement_year) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked). Explanations show both component rates because uACR is usually limiting. The clinic sample uses the same year filter, groups by Clinic, selects MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`) and MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`), and orders by Clinic.

snippets.headline: KED measures kidney health evaluation using both eGFR and uACR testing requirements for eligible diabetes patients.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: The business term `KED` means kidney health evaluation. For rows where `gold_adherence_ked.status = 'NOT_MET'`, classify the care gap exactly as follows: when `NOT egfr_flag AND NOT uacr_flag`, use `'No eGFR and no uACR'`; when `NOT uacr_flag` otherwise, use `'No uACR test'`; otherwise use `'No eGFR test'`. The KED compliance rate is based on `AVG(CAST(numerator_flag AS INT))` across the KED eligible rows, while the gap classification uses the two component flags.

snippets.headline: Matched eGFR codes identify codes actually observed during the reporting year, rather than every code included in a terminology version.
snippets.content: For each terminology version, `codes_matched` is `concat_ws(', ', collect_set(o.loinc_code))`, representing distinct codes actually present in matching observations, not the version's full eligible code list. The supporting observations in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` are restricted to `year(result_ts) = 2026`; terminology `measurement_year` remains an independently grouped version dimension. The dependency starts with distinct `measurement_year AS vs_year` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` restricted to `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`, LEFT JOINs to that same table's codes restricted to the same segment on `vs.vs_year = v.vs_year`, and LEFT JOINs to the filtered observations on `o.loinc_code = vs.code`. These LEFT JOINs preserve versions without matching observations, and `collect_set` excludes nulls and deduplicates observed codes despite code-to-observation row multiplication. The jointly reported patient measure is `COUNT(DISTINCT o.patient_id)` grouped by `v.vs_year`, so it counts patients rather than matched codes or joined rows.

snippets.headline: Each terminology version reaches observations only through its version-specific KED_EGFR codes, with unmatched versions preserved during coverage reporting.
snippets.content: The complete reusable relationship is: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` supplies distinct `measurement_year` versions filtered by `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`; that table is then LEFT JOINed back to itself on `measurement_year` and the same `segment_id` to retrieve the version's `code`; the resulting code rows are LEFT JOINed to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` on `silver_observation.loinc_code = value_set_segment.code`, with the observation-side predicate `YEAR(silver_observation.result_ts) = 2025` in the join condition. The first self-join can multiply one version row by its codes, and the observation join can multiply code rows by observations, so downstream patient coverage must use `COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)` rather than a raw row count. Filtering `measurement_year = '2026'` after the version/code construction selects that version while retaining its unmatched version row under the LEFT JOIN semantics.

snippets.headline: KED_EGFR coverage requires a version-to-code-to-observation path, with distinct patient counting preventing repeated observations from inflating results.
snippets.content: The complete relationship path is: `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` is first reduced to distinct `measurement_year` values, then `LEFT JOIN`ed to another copy of the same table on `vs.vs_year = v.vs_year` to obtain that version’s `code`, and then `LEFT JOIN`ed to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` on `o.loinc_code = vs.code`. The observation join also applies `YEAR(o.result_ts) = 2025` in the observation subquery, while the terminology copies are both restricted to `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`. A version can have multiple codes and a code can match multiple observations, so this is a one-to-many path with potential row multiplication; use `COUNT(DISTINCT o.patient_id)` at the version grain rather than counting joined rows.

snippets.headline: KED_EGFR coverage uses only the segment’s explicitly listed codes and preserves versions with no matching observations.
snippets.content: Scope the terminology table with `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`; do not treat codes from other segments as part of this value set. The complete code membership is whatever rows in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` satisfy that segment filter, separately by `measurement_year`; no literal code list is supplied. The version list is built with `SELECT DISTINCT measurement_year`, and a `LEFT JOIN` preserves every discovered version even when no 2025 observation matches, producing a zero distinct-patient count rather than removing that version.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation compliance requires both kidney tests among diabetic adults, and missing either test constitutes a care gap.
snippets.source: (Clone) [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: KED means Kidney Health Evaluation for diabetics aged 18-85 with BOTH an eGFR and a uACR test; the text identifies uACR as usually the limiting component. Patient-level clinic/panel compliance on eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked is COUNT_IF(egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*), with all patient rows in the selected breakdown as denominator. Care-gap counts are COUNT_IF(NOT (egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)). The standalone gap example equivalently uses COUNT(*) with an INCLUDE filter WHERE NOT (egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL).

snippets.headline: EGFR patient coverage is measured separately for each KED_EGFR value-set version using observations recorded during 2025.
snippets.content: For each distinct `measurement_year` version in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` where `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'`, the patient coverage metric is `COUNT(DISTINCT o.patient_id)`. Matching observations come from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation` with `YEAR(result_ts) = 2025`, and an observation matches when `o.loinc_code = vs.code`; the observation year is fixed at 2025 for every value-set version. The result is grouped by value-set version, so the metric answers how many distinct patients had an observation whose code belonged to each version's KED_EGFR code set.

snippets.headline: KED care gaps identify patients missing either kidney test, with the latest measurement year and a specific clinic scope.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: For a KED kidney-testing care-gap worklist for clinic `CLINIC-08`, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked` aliased as `k`. Restrict to the latest year with `k.measurement_year = (SELECT MAX(measurement_year) FROM eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked)`, include only rows where `NOT (k.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND k.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL)`, and filter `k.clinic_id = 'CLINIC-08'`. Derive `gap_reason` as `No eGFR or uACR test` when both dates are null, `No eGFR test` when only `egfr_datetime` is null, and `No uACR test` otherwise. Return `patient_id`, `clinic_id`, `panel_id`, `age`, both test values and dates, and order by `k.egfr_value ASC NULLS LAST`.

snippets.headline: eGFR tested patients count eligible people with at least one eGFR test during the measurement year.
snippets.content: On `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics`, `eGFR Tested Patients` counts eligible patients with a non-null eGFR test date; its definition-time expression is `COUNT(1) FILTER (WHERE egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL)`. Query the predefined measure as `MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`)` with `GROUP BY ALL`, for example: `SELECT `Measurement Year`, MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) AS `egfr_tested_patients` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`. This is the eGFR component count, not the full KED numerator.

snippets.headline: The measure dimension identifies KED as the HEDIS kidney-health evaluation measure represented by this metrics view.
snippets.content: The exposed dimension `Measure` is mapped from source `measure_id` and identifies the HEDIS measure code; this view reports KED, meaning Kidney Health Evaluation. Query the exposed dimension `` `Measure` `` when results need an explicit measure label, rather than relying only on the asset name. Example: `SELECT `Measure`, MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`) AS `ked_compliance_rate` FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_semantic`.`ked_compliance_metrics` GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: eGFR and uACR test rates are separate component measures, while KED compliance requires both tests together.
snippets.content: Two component rates answer separate questions from the full KED rate. `eGFR Test Rate` measures the share with an eGFR test and is queried as `MEASURE(`eGFR Test Rate`)`; its definition-time formula is `MEASURE(`eGFR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)`. `uACR Test Rate` measures the share with a uACR test and is queried as `MEASURE(`uACR Test Rate`)`; its definition-time formula is `MEASURE(`uACR Tested Patients`) / MEASURE(`Eligible Patients`)`. The full-measure question instead uses `MEASURE(`KED Compliance Rate`)`, which requires both tests and cannot be replaced by either component rate; query selected measures with dimensions and `GROUP BY ALL`.

snippets.headline: Kidney evaluation worklists include patients missing either required test, with reasons identifying the absent kidney testing evidence precisely.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: In eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked, INCLUDE gap patients using NOT (gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL). The matching reason is CASE WHEN gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NOT NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NOT NULL THEN 'Met' WHEN gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NULL AND gold_adherence_ked.uacr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR or uACR test' WHEN gold_adherence_ked.egfr_datetime IS NULL THEN 'No eGFR test' ELSE 'No uACR test' END. These patient-level rules mirror the KED metric view; gold rows already belong to its denominator.

snippets.headline: Patients lost compares 2025 and 2026 KED eGFR coverage counts while holding the observation measurement year fixed at 2025.
snippets.content: The comparison defines `coverage_2025` as `MAX(CASE WHEN value_set_version = '2025' THEN patients_with_egfr END)` and `coverage_2026` as `MAX(CASE WHEN value_set_version = '2026' THEN patients_with_egfr END)`, where each input is a distinct-patient count grouped by value-set version. `patients_lost` is exactly `coverage_2025 - coverage_2026`. Both coverage values are derived from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment` joined to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_observation`, with `segment_id = 'KED_EGFR'` and `year(result_ts) = 2025`; the comparison changes the terminology version, not the observation-year cohort.

snippets.headline: The metrics view is sourced from the gold adherence table, while its exposed measures should be queried through the view.
snippets.content: The underlying source is `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_ked`, which supplies the patient-level adherence records and source fields used by the metric definitions. The business metrics are exposed by `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.ked_compliance_metrics`; use that metrics view for KED measures rather than bypassing it and aggregating source rows yourself. Source-only fields such as `egfr_datetime` and `uacr_datetime` belong to the underlying source definition and should not be assumed to be queryable columns of the metrics view.

## eGFR: which measures use it, the MY2026 codes, and where they're defined

**KED (Kidney Health Evaluation) is the only quality measure that uses eGFR. For MY2026, one LOINC code counts as eGFR: `98979-8` (CKD-EPI).** For MY2025, two codes counted: `33914-3` (MDRD) and `98979-8`. [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_e60be1) Two care-protocol medication rules also use eGFR thresholds, but they aren't quality measures. [Earlier eGFR question](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/eeb38a3a26cf4d9a90f2394dcf98be5f?o=7474653847172668)

### Where eGFR is used

| Where | How eGFR is used | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **KED** (patients with diabetes, ages 18–85) | One of the two numerator tests. A patient needs both an eGFR and a uACR test in the year. It appears as `egfr_flag` in `gold_adherence_ked` and as the `eGFR Test Rate` and `eGFR Tested Patients` metrics. | Protocol rule `KED monitoredBy LP-EGFR`, section "CP sec5" [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_c17216) [KED (Kidney Health Evaluation)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/2917aa8e-38e0-48a0-90b5-040c2931541a?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668) [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-b8b53658-03e0-4831-9241-26c62476f047) |
| Metformin (biguanide class) | Not allowed when eGFR < 30 | Protocol section "CP-GLY-2" [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_c17216) |
| SGLT2 inhibitors | Not allowed when eGFR < 20 | Protocol section "CP sec4" [Query Result](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/chat/threads/a57cc2ab04a2425899ab01fe07da4667?o=7474653847172668#embed-query_c17216) |

GSD, SPD, BPD, eye exam and MAD don't use eGFR.

### Where it's defined
- **Code list:** the `KED_EGFR` segment of the value-set table [eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/explore/data/eli_test_classic_catalog/care_protocol_terminology/value_set_segment?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668). Each row is tied to a measurement year, and the MY2026 row is labeled "MY2026 modernized: CKD-EPI only". You match codes on `loinc_code = code` for the segment and year you want. [Knowledge snippet](#snippet-edda8620-a170-4029-82f4-21a22de79a49)

[eGFR (Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate)](https://fevm-eli-test-classic.cloud.databricks.com/one/discover/pages/150dfd59-85b9-4efd-8014-bb170bfe626e?isDbOne=true&utm_source=one-chat&o=7474653847172668)

It would only matter if you look back at results from 2022 or earlier.
- **2026 data exists.** The skill notes say the data covers MY2025 only, but the lab table has 2026 results.

snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: This agent has no diagnosis, medication-order, or protocol-rule tables. Comorbidity counts, contraindications, and recommended therapy questions are out of scope. Lab-result analysis is available by LOINC concept through eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.lab_result_metrics, but the supplied portion defines no named lab measures.

snippets.headline: Statin contraindication analysis connects a patient’s statin medication and diagnosis through protocol rules and terminology closures.
snippets.content: For a patient-specific contraindication result, begin with statin medications from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med` and retain rows whose `rxnorm_code` is a descendant of `DRUGCLASS-STATIN` in `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure` (`rc.descendant_code = m.rxnorm_code AND rc.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'`). Join those medications to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges` restricted to `subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'`; the edge’s `object` is the contraindication rule. Then join `protocol_edges.object` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment.segment_id`, require `code_system = 'ICD10CM'`, join `value_set_segment.code` to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.icd10_closure.ancestor_code`, and join `icd10_closure.descendant_code` to the patient diagnosis `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition.icd10_code`. This complete path requires every hop; the medication-to-rule combination uses `JOIN ... ON TRUE`, so multiple patient statins and applicable contraindication edges can multiply rows and should be deduplicated when counting unique findings.

snippets.headline: Care protocol analyses reduce diagnosis and medication evidence to patient-level facts before assessing regimen coverage or contraindication overlap.
snippets.content: Care protocol analysis uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition for diagnosis evidence, eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med for medication-order evidence, and terminology tables in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology to normalize diagnosis and drug codes. Reusable outputs in these patterns are patient-level flags, not order-level or diagnosis-row-level facts: medication and condition rows are reduced to one row per `patient_id` with `SELECT DISTINCT`, `GROUP BY patient_id`, or `MAX(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)`. This patient-level reduction is necessary before joining conditions to medications because both source tables can have multiple rows per patient and otherwise can fan out counts. The same sources support two recurring business questions: cardiorenal regimen coverage and patients on statins with contraindication diagnoses.

snippets.headline: Drug-class contraindication reports count distinct affected patients for each contraindication segment and collect matching diagnosis codes.
snippets.content: General drug-class contraindication reports are grouped at the `(drug_class, segment_id)` grain and compute `count(DISTINCT meds.patient_id) AS patients` plus `collect_set(dx.icd10_code) AS codes`. Medication rows are first reduced to distinct `patient_id`, `ancestor_code AS drug_class`, and `rxnorm_code` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med` joined to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure`, with drug classes INCLUDED by `c.ancestor_code LIKE 'DRUGCLASS-%'`. Contraindication rules are INCLUDED by `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'`, and contraindication value-set segments are INCLUDED by `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment.segment_id LIKE 'CONTRA%'`. Diagnoses are deduplicated to distinct `patient_id, icd10_code` from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx`, then matched with `dx.icd10_code LIKE concat(contra.code, '%')`; without the distinct CTEs, repeated medication orders or repeated diagnosis rows can inflate the patient counts.

snippets.headline: Contraindication analysis links medications to drug classes, class rules, coded value sets, and patient diagnoses.
snippets.content: Contraindication analysis uses a complete INNER JOIN path from medications to classes, class rules, value-set codes, and patient diagnoses. Start with `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m` JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure c` ON `m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code`, then JOIN contraindication rules from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges r` ON `r.subject = c.ancestor_code` with `r.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'`, then JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment v` ON `v.segment_id = r.object`, then JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx dx` ON `dx.patient_id = m.patient_id` and an ICD prefix condition such as `dx.icd10_code LIKE concat(v.code, '%')`. All joins are row-dropping INNER JOINs: orders without a closure mapping, classes without a contraindication rule, rules without value-set codes, and patients without matching diagnoses are removed. `rxnorm_closure`, `protocol_edges`, and `value_set_segment` can fan out a medication into multiple classes, segments, or diagnosis-code prefixes, so patient metrics should count distinct patients or pre-deduplicate patient/class/segment rows.

snippets.headline: Statin contraindication overlap counts distinct statin users who also have a matching contraindication diagnosis.
snippets.content: The statin-with-contraindication count is a patient-level intersection between statin users from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med and contraindication diagnoses from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.silver_condition. One supported statin-user path is `care_order_med.rxnorm_code = rxnorm_statin.rxcui` using eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_statin, followed by `SELECT DISTINCT patient_id`. Contraindication codes come from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges where `lower(subject) LIKE '%statin%' AND lower(predicate) LIKE '%contraindicat%'`, selecting `object AS code`, and diagnosis evidence matches `silver_condition.icd10_code = code OR silver_condition.snomed_code = code`. The metric is `COUNT(DISTINCT patient_id)` after joining the two patient sets on `patient_id`; do not count medication rows or diagnosis rows.

snippets.headline: Closure-based statin identification expands statin lookup codes to descendant medications before deduplicating patients.
snippets.content: The closure-based statin contraindication path expands statin lookup codes before finding statin users. Join eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_statin to eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure with `rxnorm_closure.ancestor_code = rxnorm_statin.rxcui`, then treat `rxnorm_closure.descendant_code` as medication `rxnorm_code` for eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.care_order_med. This path can match child RxNorm codes under statin lookup ancestors, unlike the direct `care_order_med.rxnorm_code = rxnorm_statin.rxcui` path. Deduplicate to `SELECT DISTINCT patient_id` before joining to contraindication diagnosis patients to avoid medication-code fanout.

snippets.headline: Statin contraindication counts include each patient once when statin therapy and a matching diagnosis both exist.
snippets.content: The statin contraindication patient count is a patient-grain metric: `COUNT(DISTINCT p.patient_id)` after intersecting statin-medication patients with contraindication-diagnosis patients. Statin-medication patients come from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med m` joined to statin descendants from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure` where `ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'` using `m.rxnorm_code = s.rxnorm_code`. Contraindication ICD codes come from `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.protocol_edges pe` joined to `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.value_set_segment vs` with `vs.segment_id = pe.object AND vs.code_system = 'ICD10CM'`, filtered to `pe.subject = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN' AND pe.predicate = 'contraindicatedWith'`. A patient has a matching contraindication diagnosis when `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx dx` satisfies `dx.icd10_code = vs.code OR dx.icd10_code LIKE vs.code || '.%'`; the final intersection joins statin patients and contraindication patients by `patient_id`.

snippets.headline: The 2026 statin-adherence review focuses on eligible patients with statins and selected contraindication-like diagnoses.
snippets.content: The statin-adherence review cohort in eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.gold_adherence_gsd is scoped by INCLUDE `measurement_year = 2026` and `eligible_flag` before joining to medication and diagnosis evidence. It joins to statin medications by `patient_id` after selecting DISTINCT statin medication rows from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med INNER JOIN eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_terminology.rxnorm_closure on `m.rxnorm_code = c.descendant_code` with `c.ancestor_code = 'DRUGCLASS-STATIN'`. Contraindication-like diagnosis evidence in that review is INCLUDED with `icd10_code RLIKE '^(Z34|O26|O15|O00|K70|K74)'` from eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_pat_enc_dx, and all joins use `patient_id`. The selected review attributes include `age`, `clinic_id`, statin names, matched contraindication diagnosis codes, and `size(any_value(dx.codes))` as the number of distinct diagnosis codes collected per patient.

snippets.headline: A patient’s medications are mapped to drug classes and the conditions or uses recommended for those classes.
snippets.content: For a patient-specific medication view, use `eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol.bronze_order_med` filtered with `m.patient_id = :pid`. The result returns distinct medication codes and labels, drug-class ancestors, and recommended-for targets. Medication display name is `COALESCE(h.name, m.description)`, so the RxNorm hierarchy name is preferred and the medication description is the fallback. The drug-class scope is restricted to closure ancestors matching `rc.ancestor_code LIKE 'DRUGCLASS-%'`, and only protocol edges with `pe.predicate = 'recommendedFor'` are included.

snippets.headline: Step-3 follow-up adherence counts closed ninety-day windows, while open obligations identify high-A1c patients still actionable during the year.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] Care Protocol — HEDIS Diabetes Quality (dev)
snippets.content: Protocol Step-3 means A1c follow-up after a high result and uses eli_test_classic_catalog.care_protocol_semantic.protocol_adherence_metrics. It counts only closed 90-day follow-up windows, with Trigger Events as the denominator. Open Obligations identify high-A1c patients still closable this year and are surfaced for action questions. Recent months are not described as a decline because their windows are not yet closed.

WITH meds AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT m.`patient_id`, c.`ancestor_code` AS drug_class, m.`description` AS drug, CAST(m.`start_ts` AS DATE) AS order_start, CAST(m.`stop_ts` AS DATE) AS order_stop
  FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`care_order_med` m
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`rxnorm_closure` c ON c.`descendant_code` = m.`rxnorm_code`
  WHERE c.`ancestor_code` LIKE 'DRUGCLASS-%'
    AND m.`start_ts` < TIMESTAMP'2026-10-31 00:00:00'
    AND (m.`stop_ts` IS NULL OR m.`stop_ts` >= TIMESTAMP'2026-10-30 00:00:00')
),
cond_hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT meds.`patient_id`, meds.drug_class, meds.drug, meds.order_start, meds.order_stop,
    'Condition' AS basis, r.`object` AS rule, r.`source`,
    concat(dx.`icd10_code`, ' ', dx.`description`, ' (onset ', CAST(dx.`onset_date` AS STRING), ', stop ', coalesce(CAST(dx.`stop_date` AS STRING),'open'), ')') AS evidence
  FROM meds
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` r ON r.`subject` = meds.drug_class AND r.`predicate` = 'contraindicatedWith'
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`value_set_segment` v ON v.`segment_id` = r.`object` AND v.`code_system` = 'ICD10CM'
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`bronze_pat_enc_dx` dx ON dx.`patient_id` = meds.`patient_id` AND dx.`icd10_code` LIKE concat(v.`code`, '%')
  WHERE dx.`onset_date` <= DATE'2026-10-30' AND (dx.`stop_date` IS NULL OR dx.`stop_date` >= DATE'2026-10-30')
),
last_lab AS (
  SELECT `patient_id`, `component_code`, `value_num`, `result_ts` FROM (
    SELECT l.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY `patient_id`, `component_code` ORDER BY `result_ts` DESC) rn
    FROM `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol`.`gold_lab_result` l
    WHERE `result_ts` < TIMESTAMP'2026-10-31 00:00:00' AND `component_code` IS NOT NULL) WHERE rn = 1
),
lab_hits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT meds.`patient_id`, meds.drug_class, meds.drug, meds.order_start, meds.order_stop,
    'Last lab' AS basis, r.`object` AS rule, r.`source`,
    concat('eGFR ', CAST(ll.`value_num` AS STRING), ' on ', CAST(CAST(ll.`result_ts` AS DATE) AS STRING)) AS evidence
  FROM meds
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` r ON r.`subject` = meds.drug_class AND r.`predicate` = 'contraindicatedWhen'
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` a ON a.`subject` = r.`object` AND a.`predicate` = 'appliesTo'
  JOIN last_lab ll ON ll.`patient_id` = meds.`patient_id` AND ll.`component_code` = a.`object`
  WHERE ll.`value_num` < CAST(r.`value` AS DOUBLE)
)
SELECT * FROM cond_hits UNION ALL SELECT * FROM lab_hits
ORDER BY basis, rule, drug_class, `patient_id`

  SELECT DISTINCT meds.`patient_id`, meds.drug_class, 'Last lab' AS basis, r.`object` AS rule, r.`source`, ll.`value_num` AS egfr, meds.order_start
  FROM meds
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` r ON r.`subject` = meds.drug_class AND r.`predicate` = 'contraindicatedWhen'
  JOIN `eli_test_classic_catalog`.`care_protocol_terminology`.`protocol_edges` a ON a.`subject` = r.`object` AND a.`predicate` = 'appliesTo'
  JOIN last_lab ll ON ll.`patient_id` = meds.`patient_id` AND ll.`component_code` = a.`object`
  WHERE ll.`value_num` < CAST(r.`value` AS DOUBLE)
),
allh AS (SELECT * FROM cond_hits UNION ALL SELECT * FROM lab_hits)
SELECT basis, rule, `source`, drug_class, COUNT(DISTINCT `patient_id`) AS patients, MIN(egfr) AS min_egfr, MAX(egfr) AS max_egfr, MIN(order_start) AS earliest_order, MAX(order_start) AS latest_order, COUNT(DISTINCT order_start) AS distinct_order_dates
FROM allh GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((basis, rule, `source`, drug_class), ())
ORDER BY basis NULLS LAST, drug_class

snippets.headline: Multiple care gap reporting counts gap records per patient across all five measures, then counts patients by gap total.

The full measure label list is 'GSD', 'KED', 'BPD', 'SPD', 'EED'. It computes COUNT(*) AS gap_count GROUP BY patient_id, then COUNT(*) AS patients GROUP BY gap_count ORDER BY gap_count. It neither filters nor groups by measurement_year and includes only patients appearing in the gap union, not zero-gap patients; gap_count counts records rather than distinct measure labels.

snippets.headline: Measure codes consistently identify the five quality domains: GSD glycemic status, KED kidney health, BPD blood pressure, SPD statin therapy, and EED eye examinations.
snippets.content: The recurring measure-code mapping is: `GSD` = glycemic status/A1c testing, `KED` = kidney health evaluation, `BPD` = blood-pressure control, `SPD` = statin therapy, and `EED` = diabetic eye exam. The SQL creates these codes as literal values while reading, rather than sourcing a measure-code column from the tables. Use these exact codes when combining the five measures with `UNION ALL` or interpreting the combined care-gap outputs.

snippets.headline: Care-gap counts group only unmet eligible patients by measure and exact clinical reason, preserving the distinction between gap types.
snippets.source: [dev eli_swanson] HEDIS Diabetes Quality — Care Protocol (dev).lvdash.json
snippets.content: Care-gap counts are computed as `COUNT(*)` after combining only rows with `status = 'NOT_MET'` from all five adherence tables, then grouping by `measure` and `gap_reason`. The complete reason mapping is: GSD → `'No A1c test in year'`; KED → `'No eGFR and no uACR'`, `'No uACR test'`, or `'No eGFR test'` according to its flags; BPD → `'BP not controlled / no reading'`; SPD → `'No statin dispensed'`; EED → `'No diabetic eye exam'`.
